For Gigaparsecs behind him, stretching to the very edges of the expanded arena space, absolutely all of existence turned into vibrant white lightning under his authority.
A sea of electrical annihilation waiting to be released.
He brought his hands down with finality, seeking to thunder all of that accumulated devastation directly onto Noah’s position and erase him from Existence entirely!
At such a critical moment, the scene continued playing in that strange slow-motion clarity.
Noah simply raised his stick with calm precision and spoke words that carried quiet satisfaction.
|Thank you for coming so close.|

Even though the might and Depth of Astrape was so terrifying that his Genesis Principle had transformed absolutely everything in the arena, even the Logos Noah had constructed, into white lightning, there remained one fundamental truth.
That Genesis Principle itself was ultimately a complex form of Logos written in The First Tongue.
And even though the visible Logos Noah had utilized were transformed into lightning alongside everything else, his Way could sense every single Phoneme comprising those linguistic structures.
All around him, hidden within the ocean of white lightning that now permeated the entire space, Noah had reformed the seven Logos of Imprisonment.
He had masked them perfectly to appear identical to the lightning surrounding them, making them completely undetectable.

At this moment, where Astrape’s descending hands would bring annihilation crashing down to ensure Noah’s death, Noah activated the veiled Logos that were now mere inches away from the thundering entity.
HUUM!
The terrifying waves of pressure and overwhelming power that Astrape was releasing instantly began to dwindle and be systematically repressed.
The seven Logos of Imprisonment activated simultaneously, wrapping around the shocked entity with binding authority.
Additional Logos manifested in rapid succession.
Multiple Logos of Absolute Separation cut Astrape off from his Civilization and Way.
Logos of Predetermined Failure ensured that any attempt to draw upon external Existence or utilize his Way would conclude in immediate collapse.
Because of the extreme closeness and proximity, Noah’s mastery expressed itself with devastating efficiency.
Tendrils of white lightning that had surrounded Astrape instantly transformed back into visible Logos and began binding him with multiplying restraints.
Noah himself took his Goad and began striking with serpentine speed.
The stick lashed out multiple times in rapid succession, each strike landing on different points across Astrape’s massive form.
With each precise impact, another portion of Astrape’s power was locked away and sealed.
The strikes looked like an intricate dance of Existence itself.
In the surroundings, the vibrant music of the festival permeated even into this expanded arena space.
The rhythm of drums, the melodic tones of Phoneme-based instruments, the harmonic chanting of The First Tongue all created an atmosphere that transformed violence into performance!
Above, the Ginnu Lifeforms were dancing with even more fervor as if everything had reached a critical precipice.
Their movements became faster, more passionate, more celebratory.
The more times Noah struck Astrape with his Goad, the dimmer and dimmer the authority of this once-terrifying being became.
No matter how desperately Astrape tried to express his Way of Fulmination, the Logos already binding him made such expression impossible.
And even when he managed to break through individual Phoneme connections in the linguistic chains through sheer force, Noah reformed them even faster than Astrape could shatter the links.
For the final strike, Noah took a batting stance with his Goad held in both hands.
He swung upward with explosive force, the stick connecting with Astrape’s bound form and launching the massive entity high into the air.
Noah’s figure flickered and appeared far above at the precise trajectory where Astrape would arrive.
He swung downward with equal devastating power, smashing the helpless entity back toward the arena floor with meteor-like velocity.
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4614: A Period of Quintessential Progress! III
paragraphs: The moment this occurred, the dance reached its conclusion.
Noah crashed down alongside Astrape like a falling star, his Goad positioned perfectly to drive into the massive chest of the defeated THE entity.
BOOM!
The impact shook the entire arena as Noah landed standing directly on the prone body of aTHE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereigntyentity.
Astrape looked up at him with eyes filled with pure incredulity and absolute shock.
This could not be happening. This should not be possible!
And yet...
Noah simply raised his Goad one final time and swung it down to strike Astrape’s head with measured force.
The instant the blow connected, Astrape’s entire form disappeared.
He was deemed defeated.
And now he was drawn directly intoTHE Infinite Desmoterionas its third official prisoner.
Only now did the dance truly end.
Outside the arena, the Ginnu Lifeforms dancing around the ritual flames howled out in celebration, their voices creating linguistic harmonics that made reality vibrate.
The Phonemes of Fire surrounding them exploded upward and formed into towering pillars of glorious multi-colored flames that reached toward the transformed sky.
Noah stood in the center of the arena with eyes shining brightly as he breathed out slowly, processing what had just occurred.
And glorious prompts began descending before his vision.
|Unquantifiable Harvest Initiated|
|You have suppressed and imprisoned a second entity of fundamentally higher Scale of Existence|
|Harvest being collected and amplified exponentially by Perpetual Harvest and The Cheating Architect|
|Resource generation continues exceeding conventional calculation parameters|
|All gains multiplied by factors beyond standard measurement|
|Sequential THE entity defeats are creating compound amplification effects|
|THE Scale Breaker - Distinction Evolution|
|Your Distinction has grown stronger through additional THE entity suppression|
|Effect Enhancement: Gap reduction when facing higher Scale entities increased from base level to amplified tier|
|THE Infinite Desmoterion- Prisoner Acquisition|
|Second THE classification prisoner successfully imprisoned|
|Active Prisoners: 3/36|
|Prisoner 1: Ozymandias (willing cooperation, perfect synchronization)|
|Prisoner 2: Raijin Katsuro, THE Monk of Ten Thousand Storms (disciplined cultivation)|
|Prisoner 3: Astrape, THE Maelstrom Thundermane (newly captured, status: resistant)|
|Maintenance Cost: 30 Rudimentary Units of Everything per 24 hours|
|Two THE entities now cultivating within The Desmoterion under 18,000x temporal dilation|
|Ozymandias continues perfecting The First Tongue and The Way of Mana and Hunger|
|Raijin Katsuro refines The Way of Heavenly Lightning under Mana influence|
|Astrape will be compelled to cultivate The Way of Fulmination under containment|
|The Way of Fulmination - Integration Initiated|
|As Astrape cultivates and refines his Way within The Desmoterion, aspects of The Way of Fulmination will gradually become accessible to you|
|His Genesis Principle of Absolute Conduction will be studied and potentially replicated|
|Estimated time for meaningful integration: Variable based on cooperation level|
|Timeline for elevating your own Singularity Principles to Genesis tier: Somewhat accelerated|
|THE Organ of Civilization- Development Surge|
|Current Development: 31.00% to 38.00%|
|Major advancement triggered by second THE prisoner acquisition|
|Maximum Prisoner Capacity: 36 to 45 entities|
|Temporal Dilation: 18,000x to 21,000x faster than external reality|
|THE Foundation of The First Tongue -Ongoing Growth|
|THE Civilizational Authority Resistance: 50% to 62%|
Oh!
The prompts were numerous as he needed to condense them somewhat.
But...
Noah absorbed all of these notifications with deep satisfaction.
TwoTHE Surface Depthprisoners now cultivating at twenty-one thousand times temporal dilation.
His progression was accelerating at rates that defied reasonable expectation!
And he was only just beginning to fillTHE Infinite Desmoterionwith captured entities who would fuel his advancement.
The dance continued.
Always forward.
He looked up and said with a smile.
|Teacher, this student wants more enemies...so send more THEs down!|
Teacher.

Never did he think a day would come where he would say this, but Ul’moreth had given him far too much as saying this distinction at least should be nothing much. After all, he didn’t think of himself to be so arrogant that he could not learn from another!
So he had called out above.
And truly, moments later...
He saw a distant cage be opened, an obsidian gold light pull something from inside it and chuck it down to the Arena!
ATHEentity who looked around with shock and confusion landed in the Arena right after.
And Noah raised his stick!
But...
Every THE entity held their own unique Way.
The words of Ul’moreth remained absolutely true that regardless of how much control Noah gained over The First Tongue, THE entities were inherently faster than him.
So he had to prepare multiple things in advance when he came to face them.
Astrape had talked in the beginning and given him critical time to set things in motion.
The next monster that he faced was an extremely cautious one.
The moment this entity landed and found itself in the setting of the expanded arena with an enemy it sensed was merely Pre-THE classification, it moved with ridiculously terrifying speed.
Speed that exceeded light by margins that made conventional measurements meaningless.
Well, even light couldn’t be used as an accurate comparison for what THE entities were capable of.
What they moved past could at most be accurately described by Planck Speed.
Planck Speed represented the theoretical maximum velocity at which any causality or information could travel through Existence.
It was the speed limit of reality itself, beyond which the very concept of "movement" ceased to have coherent meaning.

To move at Planck Speed meant crossing a Planck Length in a single Planck Time unit. In practical terms, it meant traversing the smallest possible meaningful distance in the smallest possible meaningful moment.
And even those words were hard to grasp as one might scratch their head!
For entities operating at this velocity, conventional space became irrelevant. Distance was no longer an obstacle but merely a suggestion that could be ignored.

In the context of their current reality where Existence itself was woven from linguistic authority and Civilizational power,Planck Speed represented movement so fast that it occurred between the individual Phonemes of a spoken Logos.
You could begin forming a word, and a THE entity moving at such velocity would cross the entire arena, strike you, and return to their starting position before the second Phoneme left your mouth.
THE entities seemingly moved even faster than this theoretical maximum.
The moment this particular entity arrived in the arena was the exact same moment it arrived directly in front of Noah with one hand already wrapped around his throat.
It was fucking terrifying!

chapters.title: Chapter 4615: Choices I
paragraphs: No transition. No visible movement. Just instant displacement from one position to another as if space itself had been deleted between the two points.
The entity’s hand clenched with crushing pressure,THE Civilizational Authorityflooding through that grip with intent to shatter Noah’s existence immediately.
Its only mistake was not moving to crush Noah’s existence or attempting annihilation in that very first instant.

Because the moment its hand made contact, the moment Noah’s existence was grabbed in close proximity, Noah used his own body as the direct conduit to layer multiple Logos of Imprisonment onto this entity’s form.
The linguistic constructs erupted from his skin where contact was made, wrapping around the shocked entity’s arm and spreading rapidly across its entire body.
While the entity processed what was happening with dawning horror, Noah began using his Goad to strike its body with rapid precision.
Each impact locked away more authority, bound more of its Way, suppressed more of its capacity to resist.
Only after seven strikes had landed and seven layers of containment were active did Noah have enough breathing room to act further.
He brought his other hand up and began manually moving the fingers of this terrifying entity, forcing them to unclasp from around his neck one by one.
The strength required was immense even with the entity suppressed, but eventually Noah extracted himself from the deadly grip.
Every single THE entity was genuinely dangerous.
Even though he had now suppressed two successfully, this third one had actually come extremely close to heavily injuring or even killing him in the opening instant.
When they stopped posturing and talking so much, when they acted with pure killing intent and maximum efficiency, THE entities were utterly dreadful opponents.
Suppressing two or three would not mean he could definitively and easily suppress others going forward.
Each one would present its own unique challenge based on their particular Way and combat approach.

But as Noah sensed this entity continuing to desperately try expressing its Way of Existence to shatter the Logos and break apart the individual Phonemes that comprised them, his eyes squinted with dangerous focus.
He utilized his Goad to continue delivering lessons with methodical brutality.
Thrashing this THE entity with strike after precise strike.
Inscribing additional containment with each blow!
Until finally, the entity’s resistance crumbled completely.
And it disappeared in the next moment, drawn directly intoTHE Infinite Desmoterionas the fourth prisoner.
Noah breathed heavily and stretched his neck with careful rotation.
Burning marks could still be felt across his throat where the entity’s hand had gripped him, only now beginning to heal under his regenerative capabilities.
After he confirmed through internal sense that everything was stable, he silently deployed multiple Logos of Imprisonment all around the arena in concealed positions.
Preparation for whoever came next.
Then he looked upward toward where he knew Ul’moreth observed and spoke with voice carrying determined hunger.
|Again!|
He didn’t even glance at the multiple prompts descending before his vision.
He simply wanted more opponents!
Outside The Primordial Genesis Arena, Ul’moreth gazed down at Noah as his student prepared to face yet another opponent.
The hairy Primeval Titan smiled beneath his obscuring hair as he turned toward a THE Intermediate Depth of Absolute Sovereignty entity standing beside him.
His voice carried casual authority as he gestured toward a specific figure below.

|Take that little fox outside of Ginnungagap and into The Infinite Unfurling. My student is extremely paranoid by nature, and while such paranoia can be exhausting, it can also be beneficial sometimes. Anomalies more often than not possess senses and instincts that the rest of us simply don’t have access to.|
He paused before continuing with thoughtful consideration.

|He says she is an investment he’s making that might pay off substantially over time, so just keep her company in The Infinite Unfurling for now while events unfold here. Take some treasures from my personal stores with you to aid her growth and advancement. Consider it my contribution to whatever my student is planning.|
Ul’moreth said all of these words while pointing toward none other than Lumivara, the nine-tailed fox who had followed Noah’s Way.
Noah had taken her out of his inner existence during the festival and spoken his final words to her with characteristic bluntness.
He wanted to continue exploring Ginnungagap and all the profound mysteries it held.
But if anything catastrophic happened during his journeys through this chaotic realm, he would be forced to utilize temporal traversal to escape immediately.
And he would not be able to take her with him if such emergency evacuation became necessary.

Since she was a follower of his Way and had sworn herself to his path, he would see what advancements she could make if she managed to survive whatever unfolded in The Infinite Unfurling on her own merit.
Lumivara had been teary-eyed but she nodded with understanding and acceptance.

At this moment, as she looked around with amazement at the ongoing battle between her Master and another THE entity, at the glorious festival continuing to unfold with ritual wonder, a Ginnu Lifeform materialized beside her.
The entity gently took her arm to whisk her away toward whatever destiny awaited beyond Ginnungagap’s borders.
While such arrangements occurred, at the distant edge of The Primordial Genesis Shore where reality began transitioning into the chaotic void, THE Fisherman sat calmly continuing his endless task.
His fishing line extended into the murky waters of Ginnungagap with patient stillness.
But his eyes pulsed occasionally with visible caution, and he sighed every few moments with increasing frequency.
As if his Weavings were tense and filled with profound worry about something he could not quite identify.
He pulled his line in once again and it came up completely empty.
No catch. Not even a nibble.
He sighed once more with building frustration.
And in that exact moment, a voice spoke from directly beside him.
|What’s got you so stressed, big guy?|
BOOM!
THE Fisherman’seyes became unfathomably grim as he whipped his head to the right.
An entity sat there casually, as if they had been present the entire time.
An entity that had somehow been here withoutTHE Fishermansensing their presence until after they chose to speak.
And they had spoken using The First Tongue with perfect fluency!

chapters.title: Chapter 4616: Choices II
paragraphs: THE Fisherman’s eyes flashed with alarm as he immediately began to-
|Come on now, don’t do any of that.|
Before Ains could even fully perceive what was happening, faster than even Plank Speed, dozens of silent Logos flashed into existence throughout the surrounding area.
The light of at least nine distinct Genesis Principles erupted simultaneously.
This entire region turned eerily quiet, reality itself seeming to hold its breath.
The urgent warning information thatTHE Fishermanwas desperately trying to send to alertUl’morethdid not even leave his existence before it was completely stopped and contained.
His eyes filled with genuine trepidation as he looked over at this being who had appeared from nowhere.
The mysterious entity seemed deceptively simple by all visual accounts.
A humanoid figure adorned in flowing robes that were perfectly split between absolute black and pure white, the division so precise it seemed to cut through the concept of color itself.
His eyes crackled with vibrant purple light that seemed to contain compressed infinity within each pupil.
His bearing felt unfathomably grand despite his relaxed posture, as if the weight of countless eons and infinite possibilities rested comfortably on his shoulders.
His eyes alone, as they gazed at everything around them with detached curiosity, held a natural superiority that would cause even weak THE entities to falter and question their own worth.
When facing such an entity,THE Fishermanfelt like...a child! As if he would be powerless regardless!
Ains stared at this being as the first words that left his mouth carried desperate need for identification.
|Which one of them are you? THE Creature? THE Primordial Chaos? THE Primordial Paradox? THE Secretive Eon? THE Tongue Whisper? THE—|
The entity laughed with genuine amusement, waving one hand dismissively.

|Relax with all those grandiose names and titles. Me, THE Creature? That brutish fucker who solves everything through raw consumption and violence? Haha, no, no. Nothing like that monstrous approach at all.|
He smiled in a manner that seemed friendly on the surface but carried unfathomable depths beneath.

|You can refer to me as THE Arbitrium. What I am is someone who seeks to learn absolutely everything about Existence and all its infinite permutations. I am also a devoted student of choices and the consequences they create. I love choices more than anything else.|
His purple eyes gleamed with building intensity.

|I consider flashy battles to be quite boring and ultimately a waste of potential. Watching the process of a choice being made, especially profoundly difficult ones where every option carries terrible cost, entertains me far more than any combat ever could. So for you, right now, there is a choice to be made.|
HUUM!
AsTHE Arbitriumsaid such words, he smiled in an overtly friendly manner and came to sit casually beside Ains as if they were old companions sharing a peaceful moment.
His voice carried terrifying weight despite the conversational tone.

|I know that your buddy Ul’moreth passed through here recently with someone unusual. I know they are currently enjoying that delightful festival inside The Primordial Genesis Shore. Which fucking sucks that you can’t even go and participate yourself, right? Stuck out here fishing endlessly while everyone else celebrates. But regardless, I know exactly what’s happening in there.|
He paused to let that sink in before continuing.

|Instead of doing some insane things that would be terribly destructive and wasteful, I want to give you a choice. A fairly simple one, all things considered. I...won’t lift a single finger to harm anyone directly. But if you choose to collapse your own Depth of Absolute Sovereignty voluntarily, if you take it all the way down from THE Fundamental Depth to merely THE Surface Depth through self-imposed destruction, if you make that choice of your own free will right now, I promise you that absolutely no harm will come to Ul’moreth.|
HUUM!
The words hung in the air with ominous finality.
This entity sat beside Ains with complete calm while delivering such a horrifying ultimatum.
Ains became even more somber as the implications crashed through his mind.
His voice emerged carefully controlled.
|What of the one that Ul’moreth traveled with?|
THE Arbitrium’ssmile widened as purple light danced in his eyes with building amusement.

|Ah, good question! I appreciate someone who thinks about all the variables before committing. If you go one step further in your sacrifice, if you completely dismantle your entire Civilization rather than merely suppressing your Depth, if you drop yourself down to before you even held any classification at all, down to just Pre-THE existence, then I won’t touch the unusual one that Ul’moreth traveled with either.|
He leaned in slightly as if sharing a secret between friends.

|And this choice I can actually help you execute if you wish to go through with it. I can ensure the process is clean and complete, no lingering fragments or hidden anchors. A true return to lesser existence. So tell me, THE Fisherman...|
His purple eyes locked onto Ains with crushing focus.
|What will it be? What will be the choice you make?|
The mysterious entity remained unfathomably calm after delivering those terrifying words.
As if they were having the most casual conversation imaginable rather than presenting Ains with a choice that would shatter his entire existence.
THE Arbitriumswung his legs with childlike playfulness as he spoke with conversational ease.

|All those years ago, you found those despicable Ginnu Lifeforms who had discovered a loophole in your community’s laws. They knew that if they outright killed any of their own kind, they would be persecuted and punished severely. So they didn’t kill. They simply slowly ate away at the existence of other Ginnu Lifeforms, keeping their victims perpetually on the edge of death and complete collapse while continuing an endless cycle of harvest on their own kind for an untold number of years.|
His purple eyes gleamed with something that might have been admiration.

|They were respected leaders in your community, trusted authorities that everyone looked up to. When you finally discovered what they were doing, you rightly and decisively collapsed every single one of them without hesitation. And in the end, you chose to keep the secret of their horrifying actions so that all Ginnu Lifeforms would not lose their fundamental faith in their leadership structure.|
He nodded with genuine appreciation.
|It was something genuinely valiant to watch unfold. Which makes it such a shame that now you have to make this new choice. Ah, the irony of Existence...|
The words caused Ains to tremble visibly as profound emotion crashed through him.
His voice emerged somber and heavy.
|Who are you really? What entity holds such knowledge of events that were buried and forgotten?|
THE Arbitriumwaved one hand dismissively, his smile never faltering.

|My specific identity is not the point here. You are missing the point entirely. The point is your choice and nothing else. So what will it be? You defended your juniors last time when it cost you dearly. Will you defend Ul’moreth and an Anomaly this time?|

|Come on now, don’t do any of that.|
Before Ains could even fully perceive what was happening, faster than even Plank Speed, dozens of silent Logos flashed into existence throughout the surrounding area.
The light of at least nine distinct Genesis Principles erupted simultaneously.
This entire region turned eerily quiet, reality itself seeming to hold its breath.
The urgent warning information thatTHE Fishermanwas desperately trying to send to alertUl’morethdid not even leave his existence before it was completely stopped and contained.

The mysterious entity seemed deceptively simple by all visual accounts.
A humanoid figure adorned in flowing robes that were perfectly split between absolute black and pure white, the division so precise it seemed to cut through the concept of color itself.
His eyes crackled with vibrant purple light that seemed to contain compressed infinity within each pupil.
His bearing felt unfathomably grand despite his relaxed posture, as if the weight of countless eons and infinite possibilities rested comfortably on his shoulders.
His eyes alone, as they gazed at everything around them with detached curiosity, held a natural superiority that would cause even weak THE entities to falter and question their own worth.
When facing such an entity,THE Fishermanfelt like...a child!
As if he would be powerless regardless!
Ains stared at this being as the first words that left his mouth carried desperate need for identification.

THE Creature?
THE Primordial Chaos?
THE Primordial Paradox?
THE Secretive Eon?
THE Tongue Whisper?
THE—|
The entity laughed with genuine amusement, waving one hand dismissively.
|Relax with all those grandiose names and titles.
Me, THE Creature?
That brutish fucker who solves everything through raw consumption and violence?
Haha, no, no.
Nothing like that monstrous approach at all.|
He smiled in a manner that seemed friendly on the surface but carried unfathomable depths beneath.
|You can refer to me as THE Arbitrium.
What I am is someone who seeks to learn absolutely everything about Existence and all its infinite permutations.
I am also a devoted student of choices and the consequences they create.
I love choices more than anything else.|
His purple eyes gleamed with building intensity.
|I consider flashy battles to be quite boring and ultimately a waste of potential.
Watching the process of a choice being made, especially profoundly difficult ones where every option carries terrible cost, entertains me far more than any combat ever could.
So for you, right now, there is a choice to be made.|

His voice carried terrifying weight despite the conversational tone.

I know they are currently enjoying that delightful festival inside The Primordial Genesis Shore.
Which fucking sucks that you can’t even go and participate yourself, right?
Stuck out here fishing endlessly while everyone else celebrates.
But regardless, I know exactly what’s happening in there.|
He paused to let that sink in before continuing.

A fairly simple one, all things considered.
I...won’t lift a single finger to harm anyone directly.

This entity sat beside Ains with complete calm while delivering such a horrifying ultimatum.

chapters.title: Chapter 4617: No longer capital!
paragraphs: THE Arbitriumleaned forward with building interest.

|Your buddy and longtime friend, I can absolutely understand why you would make that sacrifice for him. But the anomaly that he came with? You don’t really know this entity at all. You have no deep attachments or shared history. Would you truly choose to go even further, to break your entire Civilization down past THE Surface Depth and into complete Pre-THE existence, for someone you barely know?|
The words hung in the air with crushing weight.
They were followed by an immense silence that seemed to stretch across eternity.
A sense of profound power mixed with deep melancholy wrapped aroundTHE Fishermanas he sat there processing everything.
At this moment, he calmly took his fishing rod and cast out another line into the murky waters.
His movements were practiced and serene despite the trembling in his hands.
His gaze held utmost serenity and terrible power as he spoke with voice carrying absolute conviction.

|Your type continues to play with Existence as if everything lies perfectly under your fingertips. Always so arrogant and prideful, as if you could do absolutely anything with zero repercussions or consequences. One of these days, entities like you and The Others will find yourselves in the exact same positions that you keep putting the rest of us in. One of these days, you will have your due. Existence always balances itself eventually.|
THE Arbitriumsmiled with genuine amusement at these words.
His carefree nature radiated outward as he nodded with easy agreement.

|You are absolutely right. Existence is vast and unfathomable beyond anyone’s complete comprehension. Who knows what will happen seconds or years from now? I may just find myself in the exact same terrible position as you currently occupy. But right now, at this specific moment, I am on the other side of this equation. So I will enjoy it thoroughly while it lasts.|
After these words, a heavy and profound silence descended.
It carried a sense of inevitable loss and mourning.
THE Fishermanspoke calmly despite the tremor in his voice.

|I will make the choice of collapsing my Civilization all the way down before even THE Surface Depth classification. If you can help me execute this, that would be appreciated. Because inherently, my Sovereignty will resist its own collapse with everything it has. I do not think I have it within my heart to carry it out completely by myself.|
The moment he said these words with finality,THE Arbitriumsmiled with expression suggesting this entire situation brought him unfathomable joy.
His eyes flashed with a sense of immensity and terrifying power, as if the wonder and satisfaction within had grown even stronger.
He spoke with voice carrying genuine curiosity.

|What a fine choice of sacrifice that is. I can understand making it for your longtime friend Ul’moreth. But why the anomaly? Why make the choice to collapse everything even further for an entity you barely know? What drives such selflessness?|
At such a direct question,THE Fishermandid not answer immediately.
He continued holding his fishing rod with both hands, his posture unchanged.
His arms trembled slightly, visibly shaking as if his entire Sovereignty was mourning what was about to occur.
His voice emerged with quiet dignity.

|Someone like you and how you view Existence would never be able to truly understand my reasoning. Let’s not waste any more time with pointless questions. The delay of the action is only torturing me further. Do what you must.|
At such words, an extremely sad and grand scene unfolded.
THE Fishermanraised his hand and plunged it directly into his own chest.
His fingers wrapped around his heart, the core of his Civilization and Sovereignty.
And he decisively crushed it.
A massive storm of Civilizational Authority sought to erupt outward in violent rejection of this self-destruction.
ButTHE Arbitriumsimply waved his hand with casual authority and caused the explosion to disappear entirely, contained before it could manifest.
He then adopted a calm expression as if wanting to help out a dear friend in need.
A past friend.
|Ah, let me assist you with the more difficult part of erasing even THE Surface Depth classification. This requires precision.|
With such words spoken gently, he tapped out with one finger towardTHE Fisherman’sform.
Ains trembled violently as crimson-gold blood instantly spurted from his eyes, nose, and mouth.
Every single ounce of his Civilization was systematically dissipated and erased.
Existence itself wailed around him in mourning, reality crying out at the loss of such profound authority.
The mysterious entity let out a calm and satisfied sigh as he observed the completion of this sacrifice.
|Ah, what a choice. What a magnificent choice indeed!|
As he said this with genuine appreciation, something else occurred behind them.
From the inner depths of The Primordial Genesis Shore, Lumivara was being led by a Ginnu Lifeform.
They flew outward together, their figures passing by and seeing only the backs ofTHE Fishermanand the mysterious entity sitting side by side.
THE Arbitriumturned toward them with perfect timing and smiled warmly.
He waved his hand as if to say a friendly hello.
Both the Ginnu Lifeform and Lumivara immediately bowed deeply toward him with instinctive respect.
The Ginnu Lifeform also looked toward Ains and nodded with visible respect and acknowledgment.
In their eyes, they saw no blood or desolation at all. Just two entities sitting peacefully side by side as if enjoying casual conversation.
The Ginnu Lifeform gently pulled Lumivara away as they disappeared into an obsidian river passageway leading out of Ginnungagap.
THE Arbitriumwatched this departure as if it was of absolutely no consequence to him whatsoever.
He stood up and carefully wiped imaginary dust from his black and white robes.
|Ah, alright then. Thank you genuinely for the choice, THE Fisherman... oh, nope, my mistake. Just "the fisherman" now. No capital letters for you anymore. Ah, very sad indeed, my friend.|
He paused before continuing with voice carrying binding authority.

|But do not worry unnecessarily. I keep my end of every bargain I make. I will not personally move to harm a single hair on Ul’moreth or the Anomaly he brought here. For now, you simply continue fishing here as per normal and don’t ruin my fun by doing anything dramatic.|

chapters.title: Chapter 4618: Imagine It!
paragraphs: After he delivered these final words, this entity tapped out with his finger once more.
Immense waves of The First Tongue erupted outward with terrifying complexity.
Dozens of Phonemes came together with perfect precision, forming into multiple complete words.
The words combined further to form an entire sentence, a sentence that wrapped around this entire region before becoming invisible and disappearing from normal observation.
A binding constructed from linguistic authority that would ensure compliance absolutely!
This entity then hummed pleasantly to himself as he smiled with satisfaction, nodded once, and took a single step directly into The Primordial Genesis Shore.
Behind him, a desolate scene remained.
The fisherman still sat there with his fishing line cast out into the murky waters.
A smiling expression remained fixed on his face, serene and peaceful.
But bloody tears fell continuously from his eyes and nose, crimson-gold streams running down his cheeks.
His heart was destroyed.
His Civilization was completely erased.
His very being, built across eons of struggle and advancement, was just collapsed down to nothing.
And he sat there fishing, still protecting those he cared about even as everything he was dissolved into memory.
On the other end...
The mysterious entity known asTHE Arbitriumdelved deeper into The Primordial Genesis Shore.
As he moved through the chaotic space, his form began to subtly change. An aura of a unique Way of Existence manifested.
A rough obsidian robe materialized around him, replacing the pristine black and white garment.
His hair enlarged dramatically, becoming wild and unruly, pulsing with contained power.
His facial features shifted and transformed, taking on a different structure entirely.
But his eyes maintained their same infinite purple depth, crackling with that same unfathomable intensity.
He appeared at the heart of The Primordial Genesis Shore and observed the ongoing festival with genuine appreciation.
A smile crossed his transformed features as Phonemes erupted around him in joyful expression.
He actually moved forward and joined directly into the circle of dancing Ginnu Lifeforms surrounding the massive bonfire of Fire Phonemes.
He danced with them, his movements creating patterns that generated melody even grander and more complex than what the others produced.
His presence felt unique among the gathered entities, carrying weight that transcended simple classification.
Moments later, the distantUl’morethfloating above while observing the Weavings unfolding in the arena below noticed this particular dancer.
His eyes flashed with sharp recognition before he laughed with warm familiarity and voiced out with booming enthusiasm.
|Haha, Mammon, you actually made it!|
The words carried the tone one would use greeting a longtime friend arriving at a celebration.
Down at the bonfire,THE Arbitrium, now known asMammonto those gathered, looked over and smiled warmly.
He took a single step and appeared instantly besideUl’morethin the space above the festival.
His smile remained as he spoke with conversational ease.

|I just came by to see what all the commotion was about. I caught up with Ains before arriving here as he seems a little...down. He sends his regards. But...it seems you have taken in something quite dangerous to this settlement.|
As he said this, he looked down toward the arena below.
What unfolded there was another impossible scene.
Multiple Logos spun around aTHE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereigntyentity who erupted with verdant leaves and tremendous storms swirling in all directions.
The entity’s Way of Nature expressed itself with overwhelming force, attempting to transform the entire arena into a primordial forest of crushing authority.
But the Logos were gradually suppressing this tremendous power, containing and binding it piece by piece.
Opposing this THE entity was a Pre-THE Existence, none other than Noah, who moved with focused intensity.
He was gloriously forming even more complex Logos with rapid precision while simultaneously striking out with his blue-gold Goad.
Each strike locked away more authority as he steadily closed the distance toward his opponent.
Ul’moreth looked at the scene below and sighed with mixture of pride and concern.
|Not any more dangerous than anything else in Existence. Just like you and me, he is simply someone trying to pioneer his own unique Way through this vast reality.|
Mammonlooked over with expression carrying deeper understanding than anyone could imagine!
He sighed with what might have been genuine worry.

|You were always like this, Ul’moreth. Hopeful to a fault. Idealistic even when reality demands cynicism. How can you say such words when you are watching what he is currently doing? When you know exactly what something like that represents?|
His purple eyes gleamed with intensity.

|You know that The Others would inevitably come for him if they learned of his existence and capabilities. I know you understand this with absolute clarity. So why are you doing this? Why take such a monumental risk?|
The words hung heavy in the air between them.
Ul’moreth kept his gaze fixed on the arena below as he became immensely calm and somber.
When he spoke, his voice carried the weight of decisions already made.

|The Ginnu Lifeforms are not so weak that we cannot defend what we choose to protect. We fight collectively and move collectively when threats arise. And I am not merely an idiotic idealist who thinks nothing can possibly go wrong. I know many things can go catastrophically wrong. I know the substantial chance of those involved in The Oldest Paradox of Existence having dangerous interest if they knew of him and what he represents. I know all of this.|
He paused before continuing with building conviction.

|Because of that knowledge, I have taken extensive countermeasures. I have reached out to the other Leaders of Primordial Genesis Shores scattered throughout Ginnungagap. You were actually next on my list to contact, but you at times go silent for eons. But since you are already here, you can simply join in with what I am planning.|
He could simply join in?
Mammonsmiled mysteriously at such casual words.
He maintained his calm demeanor as he spoke with deceptive lightness.
|You think gathering entities like me will be of any substantial help against those disastrous beings if they decide to act? That seems optimistic even for you.|
He said such words casually, as if discussing weather rather than potential conflict with the most powerful entities in all of Existence.
Ul’moreth’sexpression revealed that he had already made a heavy choice!
|I have been thinking extensively that maybe... I should throw my full weight behind him. Completely and without reservation.|
BOOM!
The declaration carried crushing significance.
He continued with voice building in passionate conviction.

|He is young, yes. Inexperienced by our standards. But what he represents is genuinely grand and unprecedented. Rarely do entities like me or you elect to choose our own Ways to fully support another being’s advancement. We are too proud, too invested in our own paths. But doing so with him? Combining our collective strength and knowledge behind his potential?|
His eyes blazed with possibility.

|We could allow him to become just like them. Like THE Creature, THE Primordial Chaos, THE Secretive Eon, and the others who stand at the absolute apex. But better than them in crucial ways. Not filled with that same baleful ambition of trying to stomp brutally over all others just to claim the top position. Imagine someone achieving the same standing of power as those monstrous entities, but without their destructive tendencies.|
BOOM!

|The Ginnu Lifeforms are not so weak that we cannot defend what we choose to protect.
We fight collectively and move collectively when threats arise.
And I am not merely an idiotic idealist who thinks nothing can possibly go wrong.
I know many things can go catastrophically wrong.
I know the substantial chance of those involved in The Oldest Paradox of Existence having dangerous interest if they knew of him and what he represents.
I know all of this.|
He paused before continuing with building conviction.
|Because of that knowledge, I have taken extensive countermeasures.
I have reached out to the other Leaders of Primordial Genesis Shores scattered throughout Ginnungagap.
You were actually next on my list to contact, but you at times go silent for eons.
But since you are already here, you can simply join in with what I am planning.|
He could simply join in?
Mammonsmiled mysteriously at such casual words.
He maintained his calm demeanor as he spoke with deceptive lightness.
|You think gathering entities like me will be of any substantial help against those disastrous beings if they decide to act?
That seems optimistic even for you.|
He said such words casually, as if discussing weather rather than potential conflict with the most powerful entities in all of Existence.
Ul’moreth’sexpression revealed that he had already made a heavy choice!
|I have been thinking extensively that maybe...
I should throw my full weight behind him.
Completely and without reservation.|
BOOM!
The declaration carried crushing significance.
He continued with voice building in passionate conviction.
|He is young, yes.
Inexperienced by our standards.
But what he represents is genuinely grand and unprecedented.
Rarely do entities like me or you elect to choose our own Ways to fully support another being’s advancement.
We are too proud, too invested in our own paths.
But doing so with him?
Combining our collective strength and knowledge behind his potential?|
His eyes blazed with possibility.
|We could allow him to become just like them.
Like THE Creature, THE Primordial Chaos, THE Secretive Eon, and the others who stand at the absolute apex.
But better than them in crucial ways.
Not filled with that same baleful ambition of trying to stomp brutally over all others just to claim the top position.
Imagine someone achieving the same standing of power as those monstrous entities, but without their destructive tendencies.|
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4619: Imagine It! II
paragraphs: Ul’morethleaned forward with building intensity.

|Imagine the possibilities that would open for Ginnu Lifeforms across all of Ginnungagap. For the advancement and protection of The First Tongue itself. For reshaping how power operates at the highest levels of Existence.|
The words carried tremendous weight and dangerous implications.
Mammonsmiled internally at hearing such bold declarations, though his expression remained carefully neutral.

|Mm, I can imagine such outcomes. I can absolutely imagine them. But the words you are saying right now are profoundly dangerous, old friend. If THE Creature, who actively seeks to encompass all of Existence under his authority, ever hears you speak like this about elevating a potential rival...|
He shook his head with what seemed like genuine concern.

|You have to be more careful, Ul’moreth. You never know who might be listening to conversations like this one. But setting that aside for the moment, you say you will throw your full weight behind him, and you expect to convince me and the other settlement leaders to do the same? Not everyone shares the same beliefs and values as you. Many would see this as foolish risk.|
At these words,Ul’morethsmiled with absolute confidence.
|Once they see him in action, they will believe. Once they witness what he can accomplish with proper support, doubt will transform into conviction. I mean, just look at him right now.|
He gestured down toward the arena.
The scene below showed theTHE Surface Depthentity with The Way of Nature becoming fully suppressed by Noah’s relentless assault.
Multiple Logos wrapped around the defeated entity as resistance finally collapsed.
And in the very next moment, the entity disappeared entirely, drawn intoTHE Infinite Desmoterionas another prisoner.
Thereafter, Noah’s valiant shout could be heard echoing across the space.
|Again!|
Without resting for even a moment, demanding the next challenge immediately.
Ul’moreth smiled brilliantly at this display of relentless drive.
He waved his hairy hand with casual authority.
In the next instant, another distant cage opened as his brilliant obsidian-gold light reached inside, plucking the entity contained within before throwing them directly into the expanded arena.
Ul’morethhad spoken freely and openly toMammonbecause to him, this was similar to when he conversed with Ains.
A friend he had known for an unfathomably long period of time across countless eons.
ToUl’moreth, that was simply whatMammonrepresented. Nothing more, nothing less.
A trusted companion he could share his thoughts with openly!
Outside The Primordial Genesis Shore, at the very edge where reality transitioned into chaotic void, a desolate scene continued to unfold.
Ains sat there with his fishing line cast out into murky waters, his posture unchanged from before.
The smile remained fixed on his face, serene and peaceful.
But crimson-gold tears continued falling from his eyes and nose, staining his features with the evidence of profound loss.
His existence felt diminished, weak in ways that should not be possible for one who had once held such tremendous authority.
Moments later, two powerful figures materialized at the edge of The Primordial Genesis Shore.
THE First Hunger and THE Living Originappeared with cautious deliberation, their senses extended outward to assess potential threats.
They observed the figure of Ains fishing with growing confusion.
Tor, THE First Hunger,spoke first with voice carrying genuine puzzlement.

"My Hunger says this place holds the most promise for finding what we seek. It is a Ginnu Settlement, and there sits a Ginnu. Though why do his eyes seem so profoundly sad when he is merely fishing? And why does he feel so terrifyingly weak for one of his kind?"
The questions hung in the air as they approached cautiously.
And when they came within a certain distance, they both stopped instantly in shock.
A terrifying type of power wrapped around this entire region, invisible but absolutely present.
Bindings constructed from authority that transcended normal classification.
THE Living Origin’sexpression shifted to alarm as she spoke with a voice holding dawning horror.
|This type of power...is something that only someone like THE Creature himself could produce! Or perhaps one of the other entities operating at that same unfathomable caliber!|
She left the rest of the words unsaid, but the implications were clear.
If there were bindings like this present, constructed with such overwhelming mastery, it meant either THE Creature or someone of equivalent power was here at this very moment.
Or had been here recently enough that their work remained active.
But why would they bind this particular Ginnu?
What purpose could such an action serve?
Tor’s expression became heavy with determination as he made his decision.
"Let us find out what has occurred here."
In the next moment, decillions of obsidian jaws manifested around him as he began to actively devour the bindings wrapping around the fisherman.
His Way of Hunger expressed itself with full force, attempting to consume the unique weavings of a language through sheer hunger!
HUUUM!
An eruption of tremendous power crashed againstToras he was knocked backward heavily.
A deep gash opened across his mouth, blood seeping from the wound.
But he did not relent, continuing to hunger for and devour whatever power was binding this region.
His jaws multiplied exponentially, attacking the bindings from countless angles simultaneously.
His eyes shone brighter and brighter with knowledge as he did so!
"The...First Tongue!"
As he systematically dismantled the linguistic prison, he andTHE Living Originbegan to see the true state of Ains beneath the concealing authority.
The blood running down his face became visible.
The complete absence of Civilizational Authority within him became apparent.
The utter devastation of his existence revealed itself.
And finally, they could hear his words, repeated over and over in desperate loop.
"Warn Ul’moreth. Warn the Anomaly. Warn Ul’moreth. Warn the Anomaly..."
Tor and THE Living Origin’sfaces both went pale with shock.
Anomaly?
It had to be him!
He was here, inside this settlement.
But an entity of the caliber ofTHE Creaturehad actually arrived here before them and done this to a guardian of the settlement.
What did this mean for what was occurring inside?!

chapters.title: Chapter 4620: Hello! I
paragraphs: Inside The Primordial Genesis Shore, as the festival continued with building fervor, another glorious battle reached its conclusion.
The Ginnu Lifeforms cheered with tremendous enthusiasm, watching yet anotherTHE Surface Depthentity disappear under the relentless might of The Scale Breaker.
In the arena, Noah stood calmly with his Goad still gripped in one hand.
He was about to raise his fist to call out for another opponent when Ul’moreth’s voice arrived directly in his ears.
|Haha, take a brief breather and come out of the arena for a moment. There is someone I want you to meet.|
SomeoneUl’morethwanted him to meet?
Noah raised his brows at this unexpected development as he gave a light nod of acknowledgment.
He had been fighting nonstop with singular focus to imprison as manyTHEentities as he possibly could in rapid succession.
Because frankly, he did not feel comfortable at this moment.
Whenever things went unfathomably well for him without interruption, he instinctively waited for the other shoe to drop.
Things had gone ridiculously well for far too long as he constantly expected Existence to come crashing down catastrophically in the next second.
He was currently operating in full caution mode, with the intricate workings of The First Tongue burning continuously across his existence in defensive configurations.
And he had even held back from observing the accumulating prompts.
But at this moment, with a brief pause granted, he called forth the full collection of notifications.
|THE Infinite Desmoterion - Comprehensive Status Update|
|Total Prisoners Contained: 15|
|Prisoner 1: Ozymandias (willing cooperation, perfect synchronization)|
|Prisoners 2-15: THE Surface Depth entities (various cooperation levels)|
|Maintenance Cost: 150 Rudimentary Units of Everything per 24 hours|
|Prisoner diversity creating exponential synergistic effects|
|Time Elapsed Within Desmoterion:More than 1,283 days |
|All prisoners have been cultivating continuously under maximum temporal dilation|
|Collective advancement creating compound acceleration effects|
|THE Organ of Civilization- Exponential Development|
|Current Development:38.00% to 59.00%|
|Major advancement triggered by reaching 15 total prisoners|
|Critical Threshold Crossed: Development acceleration has entered exponential phase|
|Maximum Prisoner Capacity: 45 to 63 entities|
|Temporal Dilation: 21,000x to 27,000x faster than external reality|
|THE Foundation of The First Tongue -Mastery Approaching Perfect Speaker|
|Mastery Classification: Fluent Speaker (Peak) - approaching Perfect Speaker threshold|
|THE Civilizational Authority Resistance: 62% to 81%|
|Logos Formation: Can now construct 12+ Phoneme Logos with zero error risk|
|Inscription Speed: Increased by 940% from baseline|
|Way Integration - Multiple Paths Consolidated|
|The Way of Heavenly Lightning: 67% to 89% integration|
|The Way of Fulmination: 41% integration achieved|
|The Way of Nature: 23% integration initiated|
|Ten Additional Ways: Various integration levels (8%-67%)|
|Your Way of Mana and Hunger are expanding to encompass aspects of all imprisoned Ways|
|Genesis Principle Analysis - Critical Milestone Approaching|
|Total Genesis Principles Observed: 14 distinct variations|
|Structural Analysis: 97% complete|
|Understanding of structure of Genesis-tier authority construction: Exceptional|

|After approximately 15 minutes of external time, enough Weavings of Genesis Principles will have been collected and analyzed to allow for the systematic alteration and elevation of current Principles to Genesis Principle classification|
|Unquantifiable Harvest - Compound Accumulation|
|Resource generation from 15 THE prisoners has exceeded all projection parameters|
|Perpetual Harvest and The Cheating Architect creating multiplication effects that defy calculation|
|All fundamental aspects of your existence growing exponentially|
|Bloodline Formation - Accelerated Crystallization|
|Lineage Emergence: 47% to 98% complete|
|The Distinction of The Early Creature, Osmont continues systematic dissolution|
|New fundamental identity crystallizing rapidly around linguistic supremacy|
|Estimated Completion: Soon? Soon.|
The prompts were glorious.

THE Foundation of The First Tongue, THE Organ of Civilization, His budding Lineage...as there was even the fact that after 15 minutes, he would be able to effectively modify his Principles into more complex Logos.
Just 15 Minutes.
After the prompts finished rolling down with their extraordinary implications, Noah kept his eyes closed to observeTHE Infinite Desmoteriondirectly.
His consciousness descended into that vast internal space.
The scene that greeted him was one of tremendous organized activity.
The sky pulsed with intensified blue-gold radiance, the color deeper and richer than before.
The ground formed from crystallized Hunger had expanded dramatically, now covering what felt like continental scale.
Throughout this vast space, fifteen distinct regions had formed, each one containing a prisoner.
Ozymandias occupied the central and largest region, his form radiating authority as he continued perfecting The First Tongue with methodical precision.
Around him in a circular arrangement, fourteenTHEentities each occupied their own designated cultivation zones.
Some remained resistant, their forms wrapped in additional layers of Logos to ensure containment.
But most had entered states of focused cultivation, either through genuine cooperation or simple acceptance of their situation.
Raijin Katsuro sat in meditation with disciplined posture, lightning crackling around him in controlled patterns as he refined his Way with obsessive dedication.
Astrape occupied another zone, still radiating defiance but unable to express it meaningfully through the containment.
The entity with the Way of Nature had transformed their entire region into a miniature forest ecosystem, using their imprisonment as opportunity to deepen understanding of growth and cycles.
Others exhibited similar adaptations, each prisoner finding ways to advance despite or perhaps because of their confinement.
And overseeing all of this with absolute authority, Ozymandias moved between regions offering guidance, corrections, and occasionally additional suppression when resistance flared.
The atmosphere felt like an academy of existential cultivation, with the most reluctant students gradually becoming the most dedicated once they accepted their circumstances.
Noah observed the flow and workings of this space with deep satisfaction.
Everything operated with beautiful efficiency.
His Way advanced with every moment that passed within this accelerated time.
He smiled with genuine appreciation for what he had built.
Then he took a single step and appeared outside the arena, back in the festival space.
Who exactly did Ul’moreth want him to meet?
Outside the arena, the festival had reached its precipice and seemed to be slowly wrapping up as Noah made his way toward Ul’moreth.
Everywhere he passed, the Ginnu Lifeforms cheered him on with genuine enthusiasm.
Some reached out to hit his body jovially in celebration, their hands thumping against his shoulders and back with friendly force.
He simply nodded back at them with quiet acknowledgment, appreciating their genuine warmth while maintaining his focus.
When he arrived before Ul’moreth, he saw that his teacher was not alone.

chapters.title: Chapter 4621: Hello! II
paragraphs: The figure of another powerful Ginnu Lifeform stood beside him.
A being that Noah immediately noted carried a heavy sense of oppression similar toUl’moreth’spresence.
If not slightly denser and more profound.
This being looked toward him with calm observation, purple eyes studying him with interest that felt both curious and calculating.
Ul’moreth waved his hand to form an isolated domain of obsidian-gold light around the three of them.
As if he didn’t want what he was about to discuss to be overheard by everyone at the festival.
He looked toward Noah and nodded with visible appreciation as he spoke with building enthusiasm.

|It seems THE Surface Depth classification is not far from your grasp at this rate of advancement. I was just telling this old friend here that I have come to a profound decision after watching your performances. To give you my complete support and backing, and to lobby actively on your behalf to others like me across Ginnungagap.|
His voice carried weight of genuine conviction.

|If multiple entities of our caliber throw our full weight behind you, if we combine our resources and authority to support your advancement, then with what you already represent and your mastery of The First Tongue, what would possibly stop you from wielding the same level of power as THE Creature or any of The Others who stand at the apex?|
Ul’moreth’swords were tremendously heavy.
Noah’s eyes shone brightly at the implications.
The full support of multipleTHE Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereigntyentities?
Such a terrifying boost seemed almosttoogoodto be true.
He had been wondering how much longer he would even be able to remain in Ginnungagap.
His timeline was to attainTHEclassification in the next few hours at the exponential rate that things were currently progressing.
And after grasping that level of power, he could move with genuine confidence to exploreTHE Vaults of Ginnungagapand claim whatever treasures they held before making his way back to his current time.
If he also had the backing and support of beings like Ul’moreth, entities who stood at the very peak of what Existence produced...
His eyes flashed as his paranoia returned with full overwhelming bloom.
That would mean things continuing to go ridiculously smooth without interruption.
The sense of profound unease in his existence grew even stronger as he looked around cautiously.
He raised his head upward as if literally expecting the fabric of Existence to shatter in the next moment and bring catastrophe crashing down.
When he did this,Ul’morethsmiled wryly at his student’s excessive caution.
Beside him, the one he had introduced as a friend looked at Noah with growing amusement and spoke with a voice of genuine curiosity.
|After being told of such grand possibilities and offered tremendous support, why is the very first thing you do looking upward with such extreme caution? Most would be celebrating.|
Noah brought his eyes down to focus on this being andUl’morethbefore he replied with calm seriousness.

|Fortune and disaster come hand in hand throughout Existence. There has been so much concentrated fortune falling upon me that my intuition is screaming warnings about potential disaster arriving to balance the scales.|
At these words,Ul’morethlaughed jovially as he clapped Noah on the shoulder.

|Being careful and cautious is genuinely good practice! But this entity here is Mammon, an old friend of mine. As long as you have him as another backer alongside a few others with our Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereignty supporting you directly, entities like THE Creature will not be a genuine danger to you in the future!|
AfterUl’morethmade this introduction, the being known as Mammon stepped forward with a warm smile.
He raised his hand casually toward Noah in offer of a handshake.
His voice carried friendly warmth as he spoke.
|I go by many names across different eras and regions. Ains knows me by one particular name, Ul’moreth knows me by another. Mammon is a longtime name of mine that I’ve grown quite fond of...|
As he said this, Noah looked at this being with close attention.
Toward the outstretched hand, he returned the handshake astheir two hands made contact.
While this physical connection occurred, Noah also activated his Lens of Civilization to examine whether this being was veiled like Ains had been or freely displaying their true capabilities.
A status sheet materialized before his vision.
|Analysis Report|
|Name: Mammon (?)|
|Classification: ???|
|Depth of Absolute Sovereignty: ???|
|Way of Existence: ???|
|Civilizational Authority: ???|
|True Nature: ???|
|Additional Title freely left unveiled:The Eldest of The Oldest Paradox of Existence|
Noah blinked as his eyes became razor sharp.
His mind buzzed with accelerating thoughts as his heart beat faster, and THE Organ of Civilization began to howl!
The Eldest of The Oldest Paradox of Existence?
The Oldest Paradox of Existence referred to the fundamental question of what came first in the origin of reality.
The chicken or the egg. Existence or The First Tongue.
Which preceded which, and how could either exist without the other already being present?
The paradoxical nature of this question gave Paradox itself tremendous power as a concept.
If someone was deemed The Eldest of The Oldest Paradox of Existence, that would mean...
HUUM!
Noah’s eyes pulsed with unfathomable somberness and building intensity!
His entire existence howled with alarm as realizations struck at Planck Speed.
The Logos branded across his body began lighting up with defensive brilliance.
In front of him, the one whose hand he was shaking smiled brilliantly as he continued speaking with voice carrying building revelation.
His words carried imposing and terrifying weight as the truth emerged.

|I go by many names, yes. So many names accumulated across eons. Mammon works perfectly well for casual interactions. THE Arbitrium serves for certain purposes. But the name I personally like the most, the one that represents what I truly am...|
He paused for perfect dramatic effect.
|...is Chaos.|
HUUM!
Everythingseemed to shift into slow motion as reality itself struggled to process what was occurring.
Noah’s expression transformed to heavy somberness as his entire existence buzzed with alarm.
Every instinct screamed danger at maximum intensity.
Mammon’s face held a brilliant, devilish smile as if everything unfolding was profoundly amusing to him.
As if this entire situation brought him tremendous entertainment.
He finished his words with that devilish smile spreading even wider.
|Chaos. THE Primordial Chaos. Hello there, Anomaly. It is so, so very nice to finally meet you properly.|
BOOM!
The words held such tremendous weight that it felt like all of surrounding Existence had literally shattered.
In this glorious scene where everything continued moving in impossible slow motion, Ul’moreth’s expression transformed through multiple stages in rapid succession.
From confusion, to shock as he processed the words being spoken, to explosive lividity as realization struck, to absolute horror as the full implications crashed through his mind.
And Noah could only gaze back with eyes blazing with brilliant, utterly defiant Quintessence.
His hand was held tightly in the grip of an unfathomable entity.
One of The Others who stood at the absolute apex of all Existence.
THE Primordial Chaos himself.
Oh.
Oh!
OH!!!
The other shoe had dropped.And it was a fucking heavy of drop!

If not slightly denser and more profound.

Ul’moreth waved his hand to form an isolated domain of obsidian-gold light around the three of them.
As if he didn’t want what he was about to discuss to be overheard by everyone at the festival.
He looked toward Noah and nodded with visible appreciation as he spoke with building enthusiasm.
|It seems THE Surface Depth classification is not far from your grasp at this rate of advancement.
I was just telling this old friend here that I have come to a profound decision after watching your performances.
To give you my complete support and backing, and to lobby actively on your behalf to others like me across Ginnungagap.|
His voice carried weight of genuine conviction.

|If multiple entities of our caliber throw our full weight behind you, if we combine our resources and authority to support your advancement, then with what you already represent and your mastery of The First Tongue, what would possibly stop you from wielding the same level of power as THE Creature or any of The Others who stand at the apex?|
Ul’moreth’swords were tremendously heavy.
Noah’s eyes shone brightly at the implications.
The full support of multipleTHE Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereigntyentities?
Such a terrifying boost seemed almosttoogoodto be true.

His timeline was to attainTHEclassification in the next few hours at the exponential rate that things were currently progressing.

If he also had the backing and support of beings like Ul’moreth, entities who stood at the very peak of what Existence produced...
His eyes flashed as his paranoia returned with full overwhelming bloom.
That would mean things continuing to go ridiculously smooth without interruption.
The sense of profound unease in his existence grew even stronger as he looked around cautiously.
He raised his head upward as if literally expecting the fabric of Existence to shatter in the next moment and bring catastrophe crashing down.

Most would be celebrating.|
Noah brought his eyes down to focus on this being andUl’morethbefore he replied with calm seriousness.

There has been so much concentrated fortune falling upon me that my intuition is screaming warnings about potential disaster arriving to balance the scales.|
At these words,Ul’morethlaughed jovially as he clapped Noah on the shoulder.
|Being careful and cautious is genuinely good practice!
But this entity here is Mammon, an old friend of mine.

As long as you have him as another backer alongside a few others with our Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereignty supporting you directly, entities like THE Creature will not be a genuine danger to you in the future!|
AfterUl’morethmade this introduction, the being known as Mammon stepped forward with a warm smile.
He raised his hand casually toward Noah in offer of a handshake.
His voice carried friendly warmth as he spoke.

Ains knows me by one particular name, Ul’moreth knows me by another.
Mammon is a longtime name of mine that I’ve grown quite fond of...|

|Name: Mammon (?)|
|Classification: ???|
|Depth of Absolute Sovereignty: ???|

chapters.title: Chapter 4622: End of The Line I
paragraphs: In Existence, more often than not, entities believed themselves to be infallible.
They accumulated power and authority and began thinking they would live forever, that nothing could truly threaten what they had built.
Many did not understand the fragility of their own mortality until the moment it was stripped away.
They moved through reality with confidence that bordered on arrogance, certain that their preparations were sufficient and their foundations unshakeable.
Then there were others who understood their own mortality with painful clarity.
Who recognized that things could and did always go wrong, regardless of how careful one was.
These entities prepared for all eventualities and considered all possibilities with paranoid thoroughness.
They did everything they absolutely could and remained as cautious as possible at every moment.
But sometimes, even after such exhaustive preparation, even after accounting for every variable and planning for every contingency, even after being as careful as an entity could possibly be...
Sometimes things just happened anyway.
Shit happened.
That was Existence, and Existence simply was.
No amount of preparation could fully protect against the truly unexpected.
Before Noah, shit had truly happened in the most catastrophic way possible.
He gazed into the eyes of this terrifying being holding his hand as nearby, Ul’moreth’s body began trembling violently.
THE Primeval Titan’shair rose up with explosive power as shockingly, his authority seemed to be surging even withinTHE Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereigntyand climbing higher.
His hidden eyes held a devastating mixture of lividity, shock, and profound feelings of betrayal all compressed into a single moment.
But before anything could be done by him, before he could act on the rage and horror flooding through his existence, Noah faced the entity before him.
And uniquely, he didn’t feel any fear.
Even though this was arguably the single most dangerous moment in his entire existence across all his life, he remained utterly calm.
His existence lost all other thoughts except singular focus onsurvival.
His eyes turned immensely cold and crystalline calm as he looked directly at this being and spoke with a voice carrying absolute conviction.

|You are unfathomably faster and stronger than me in every measurable way. But you are not faster than my own thoughts. You are not faster than my own tongue. You are not faster than The First Tongue itself when spoken from within my existence.|
His words carried building intensity.

|Should you move to do anything hostile to me in the next moment, my thoughts will move instantly. The First Tongue will move. And with it, I will initiate something irreversible that will doom all of Existence to collapse. Not just you or me, but everything.|
BOOM!
His words emerged without any trace of fear! He made a bold claim that he could initiate the doom of all of Existence!
His eyes shone with the brilliance of pure Quintessence, with tyranny and absolute defiance even when facing this apex entity.
This being who continued holding his hand in what was unquestionably the longest and most dangerous handshake in all of Existence.
And toward Noah’s bold declaration, this entity actually had his purple eyes shine with tremendous brilliance.
He smiled with what seemed like genuine delight as he responded.

|Why would I do anything bad to you? I came here purely because I was curious. And my friend Ul’moreth, pipe down and do not ruin my curiosity with your explosive temper. I’ve already grabbed hold of his existence, and I could do...many things.|
His smile widened.
|Even though you do not truly know me personally, you should understand at least a glimpse of my power from reputation alone. So why don’t we all just relax and have a pleasant conversation? Haha...|
Ul’moreth’sbody continued showing surging Weavings of Existence and overwhelming emotion.
His entire form trembled with contained power that wanted desperately to erupt.
But at this moment, he remained frozen in place, unable to move despite his tremendous authority.
Held perfectly still by power that transcended what even he could resist.
The eyes ofTHE Primordial Chaosshone with unfathomable depth and concentrated power.
Within those purple depths, endless Weavings of pure Chaos churned and shifted in patterns that defied comprehension.
Before Noah’s vision, terrifying and ominous prompts materialized.
|CRITICAL EXISTENTIAL CHALLENGE|
|Your Way of Existence and all aspects of your being have come across an unstoppable force of Existence itself|
|Your Way is being fundamentally tested at its deepest level|
|At this moment, the entirety of your existence and your Way is being challenged by The Oldest Paradox of Existence itself|
|Question Posed:|
|Before THE Primordial Chaos, what are you?|
|This question demands answer not through words but through the fundamental structure of your existence|
|Failure to maintain coherent answer will result in existential dissolution|
WAA!
What was he?
BeforeTHE Primordial Chaos, what was Existence itself, and what was The First Tongue?
Which came first, and how could either exist without the other?
The sensation Noah felt in this moment was utterly indescribable.
He felt every single atom and cell of his existence working in absolute overdrive.
As if every single component part of what made him real was being questioned again and again in rapid succession.
Before THE Primordial Chaos, whatwashe?!
What defined his existence when confronted with the living embodiment of paradox?
The questions boomed through his mind with crushing weight as the entity in front of him continued smiling pleasantly during all of this existential pressure.
THE Primordial Chaosspoke with voice carrying both amusement and genuine fascination.

|What an enigma you are, truly. You do not belong here in Ginnungagap and yet you absolutely do. You should not be here by any logical progression and yet you undeniably are. You are weak by classification and yet you are also profoundly strong in application. You have so many paradoxes surrounding your entire existence that I would have genuinely thought you were THE Living Paradox in a different form if I didn’t know better.|
He paused before continuing with building interest.

|But no matter. I am not here for anything too crazy or destructive. I am here simply to ask a few specific people to make choices. I asked Ains to make a choice a little bit earlier at the edge of this settlement, and he made it decisively. What a selfless individual he was, choosing sacrifice over safety.|
His purple eyes gleamed.

|I will now ask you what choice you will make when presented with options. Nothing wild and nothing unreasonable. You spoke of me potentially doing something hostile or even expecting destruction from my presence, but I find such direct violence tedious and profoundly boring most of the time.|
His smile took on deeper significance.

|I find Existence to be vastly more interesting when everything is based on choices made freely. On the glorious Primordial Chaos that blooms naturally as a result of endless choices intersecting and creating unpredictable outcomes. Force is simple. Choice is beautiful.|
The words hung in the air with tremendous weight.
What choice wouldTHE Primordial Chaosdemand from him?
